DIAGNOSIS READY: Cholangiocarcinoma (specifically affecting the distal common bile duct).

The clinical picture of obstructive jaundice, weight loss, and a cystic mass causing bile duct dilation is highly suggestive of a malignant biliary stricture. The normal liver enzymes (AST/ALT) with elevated alkaline phosphatase and direct bilirubin further supports a primary biliary obstruction rather than hepatocellular disease.
